rules.statement: Code that creates a row on demand must tolerate a concurrent creator: when the insert fails on a duplicate key, re-read the existing row rather than surfacing the error.
rules.why: Lazy, on-demand creation can race between concurrent requests, and the loser of the race should still end up with the created entity.
rules.check: Look for get-or-create paths that insert after a missing read and either let the duplicate-key failure propagate or don't re-read the row after a failed insert.

rules.statement: A seed contributor must be idempotent, so running it again against an already-seeded tenant changes nothing and does not fail.
rules.why: Seeding runs again on every tenant cache miss, for the tenant and for the root tenant, so that contributors added later reach existing tenants.
rules.check: Look for seed contributors that insert without checking for existing data, that create duplicates, or that throw when their data already exists.

rules.statement: A seeder that grants privileged credentials or well-known accounts must target one tenant named explicitly in configuration, must not fall back to a default or to every tenant, and must have its options validated so the host refuses to start when the name is missing.
rules.why: A fallback to all tenants would give every tenant created at runtime clients carrying GlobalAdmin, a well-known administrator, or test-suite credentials, and a default that changes with the strategy is a silent guess.
rules.check: Look for seeder options whose tenant id is optional or defaults to the root, static, or all tenants, and for missing startup validation of those options.

rules.statement: Lazily create only the tenants that configuration defines; a request for any other tenant that does not exist must return 404 and must not create it.
rules.why: Tenants other than configuration-defined ones are created only through the management API; creating them from request resolution would let any request bring a tenant into existence.
rules.check: Look for tenant-resolution code that inserts a tenant for an unknown id or path instead of returning not found.

rules.statement: A management create endpoint must finish provisioning or seeding the new tenant before it responds, and its response must carry the entity as it stands after that work.
rules.why: The tenant's system resources have to exist before its first request, and seeding may change the row, so the response should show the final state.
rules.check: Look for create endpoints that return before running seeding, or that return the object as it was before seeding instead of re-reading it.

rules.statement: Run tenant seeding only on a tenant cache miss, never on every request.
rules.why: Some strategies resolve the tenant on every request before they can check the cache, so seeding during resolution would seed on every request.
rules.check: Look for seeding or provisioning calls in per-request tenant resolution paths that run outside the cache-miss factory.
